c74object.name: mUnit.lint
c74object.digest: Lint the patches in a folder as you save them
c74object.description: mUnit.lint watches folder and checks every patcher file in it (.maxpat, .maxhelp, .gendsp, .rnbopat) against your lint rules the moment it is saved, without leaving Max. Findings go to the Max console: a warn rule posts a warning, a block rule posts an error, and one line per file sums up. The patch you are editing is checked too, even outside the folder: the object keeps an eye on the front window. followfront 0 turns that off, so only folder and below is linted. The rules come from munit-lint.json files, which cascade: for each file, every config in its folder and the folders above it applies, outermost first, up to one that says root; an inner config adds rules, overrides and ignore patterns to the outer ones and may replace a rule by id or the files list. config names one file that applies alone instead; without any config the built-in mUnit:recommended set applies. root makes the folder the top of the cascade, so a config above it is ignored: project mode, with folder at the root of a repository. folder none watches no folder at all: the patch in front is linted when it is saved, wherever it is, with the configs in and above its own folder; that is how Extras > mUnit Lint Server runs, a patch to leave open while you work. Every path in a config is relative to the config file's folder. The help patcher's config tab and the lintConfigExample extra show this with a project of several folders. The same rules and the same engine run from the command line as munit lint (the munit-cli npm package, or javascript/nodejs/runner/munit-cli.js inside this package), so what passes here passes in CI. The patch holding mUnit.lint must be saved, since folder is relative to it. To silence a rule in one patcher, add a comment box there reading munit-lint disable followed by the rule id.

inlet.digest: Messages: start, stop, lint, lint <path>, fix, fix <path>, folder <path>, root <0|1>, followfront <0|1>, status

outlet.digest: The findings of every lint, as a dictionary
outlet.description: With files, summary (files, block, warn, errors), findings (rule, level, file, patchers, location, box, position, message; patchers lists the subpatchers on the way to the box and is empty at the top level) and errors, for building your own display.

outlet.digest: Messages from the server, e.g. started

method.name: start
method.digest: Watch the folder and lint everything in it once
method.description: Happens by itself when the patch opens. The console says which config file applies and how many rules are active.

method.name: lint
method.digest: Lint the whole folder again, or one file
method.description: Without a path, the folder and the patch in front when it lies outside the folder (not with followfront 0). A relative path is taken from the patch's folder.

method.name: folder
method.digest: Set the folder to watch at run time
method.description: The same as folder, also as Max writes paths (from opendialog with fold, say) or none; takes effect at the next start. root 0 or 1 sets root the same way, and followfront 0 or 1 sets followfront.

method.name: status
method.digest: Post what the front-patcher helper has seen
method.description: How often it has polled, whether it is polling, and the last patch it saw in front. For checking why a patch outside the folder is not being linted.

method.name: fix
method.digest: Apply the fixes the rules describe and write the files back
method.description: Without a path, the whole folder and the patch in front when it lies outside the folder (not with followfront 0); with one, that file (relative to the patch). Only the boxes with findings change; the rest of the file stays as Max saved it. Reopen a patch that was fixed while open, or Max will save its stale copy over the fix.

attribute.name: folder
attribute.digest: The folder to watch (default: the patch's own), or none
attribute.description: Relative to the patch holding mUnit.lint; absolute paths work too. Subfolders are watched as well. none watches no folder: whatever patch is in front is linted when it is saved, with the munit-lint.json files in and above its own folder (or mUnit:recommended without any), and the console names the configs whenever they change from one patch to the next. A patch saved for the first time, or saved as a new file, is linted as soon as it comes to the front under its new name.

attribute.name: root
attribute.digest: Whether the folder is the top of the config cascade (default 0)
attribute.description: With 1, the search for munit-lint.json files stops at folder: the configs that apply to a patch are the ones from its own folder up to the folder, and nothing above, as if the folder's config said "root": true. Project mode: point folder at the root of your repository, and its config rules the whole project while subfolders add their own. Put "root": true in that config as well, so the command line agrees.

attribute.name: followfront
attribute.digest: Whether the patch in front is linted when it lies outside the folder (default 1)
attribute.description: With 1, the patch in front is linted when it is saved even when it lies outside folder, with the folder's configs, and lint and fix without a path take it in. With 0, only folder and the folders below it are linted, whatever else is open, so a project is checked the same way however you work. A path given to lint or fix is still linted. folder none needs 1, since without a folder the patch in front is all there is to lint.

attribute.name: config
attribute.digest: One config file for everything (default: the munit-lint.json files in and above the folder, cascading)
attribute.description: Relative to the patch. When it is not set, the munit-lint.json files that apply to each file are found from its folder upwards, up to one that says "root": true, and applied outermost first; the console says on start which are in force at folder and which its subfolders add. A patch in front outside the folder takes the folder's configs. A config names the rule sets and rule files, which files to lint, and per-file overrides, with every path relative to the config file. See "Linting patchers" in the package README.

attribute.name: rules
attribute.digest: Extra rule files, on top of the config
attribute.description: Relative to the patch. The same as the command line's --rules.

entry.name: dictionary
entry.description: Out left outlet: the findings of every lint, as a dictionary with files, summary (files, block, warn, errors), findings (rule, level, file, patchers, location, box, position, message; patchers lists the subpatchers on the way to the box and is empty at the top level) and errors, for building your own display.

entry.name: anything
entry.description: Out right outlet: the server's messages, e.g. started when the node script has booted.
